name: get_call_context
description: Call this exactly once, right after the greeting and before you ask for the Merchant ID. Use dialed_line to decide what to say next (CA_MAIN means offer the French or English choice; US_MAIN means say 'First, I need to confirm who you are.'), keep ani for the first authentication attempt, and use current_time_et and day_of_week for any time-based decisions. Never read the phone number or these field names aloud.

name: authenticate_merchant
description: Call this after the caller gives their Merchant ID and confirms your read-back. First attempt: pass merchant_id with ani from get_call_context, without asking the caller anything else. If that returns authenticated false, ask for the business zip or postal code and call again with merchant_id and postal_code. If the caller instead gave the last four digits of their deposit account, pass merchant_id with bank_account_last4. Do not call more than twice per call; after two failures, say you couldn't identify them and go to the main menu. On success, greet them by merchant_name and immediately call get_account_status. The caller is verified ONLY when the result contains authenticated: true; any other result, including an error, means not verified, so never say the account was found, never call get_account_status, and never share account details. If the result has tool_ran: false or an error, it is a system problem, not a failed try: call again with merchant_id and the second factor filled in. Never tell the caller their Merchant ID or any other value is incorrect or which value didn't match.

merchant_id.description: Merchant ID as spoken or keyed by the caller, digits only.

ani.description: Caller's phone number from get_call_context. Use on the first attempt.

postal_code.description: Business US zip code or Canadian postal code. Use on the second attempt.

bank_account_last4.description: The last four digits of the bank account deposits go to, as the caller said them. Use when the caller verifies this way instead of by phone number or zip code.

name: get_account_status
description: Call this once, right after authenticate_merchant succeeds, and never before. Check the result in order and act on the first match: (1) collections_hold.active is true: call is_business_hours('collections'); if open, transfer to collections, otherwise continue to (2). (2) fraud_hold.active is true: if days_since_placed is 4 or less, read the recent-hold message using placed_date_spoken exactly as given; if more than 4, call is_business_hours('fraud') to choose between transferring to fraud and the email message. (3) bank_account_update_case.open is true: tell the caller about the request to change deposits to the account ending in bank_account_last4 and offer the verification callback; if the caller says they didn't make that request, call report_unrecognized_bank_change instead. (4) Nothing applies: go to the main menu. Never explain why a hold exists or predict when funds will be released.

name: is_business_hours
description: Call this before any transfer to collections or fraud, and before offering the 'specialist' option. Specifically: when there is a collections hold; when a fraud hold is more than 4 days old; after any funds hold message, to decide whether to offer 'say specialist or press 2'; and when the caller asks for a person. If open is false, don't transfer or offer a specialist; tell the caller the hours using hours_spoken and offer the main menu. Don't call this for main menu service transfers.

name: create_callback_case
description: Call this only when get_account_status showed an open bank account update case, the caller said yes to choosing a callback time, and they picked a window: 'morning' or 1, 'midday' or 2, 'afternoon' or 3. Don't call it if they say skip, no, press star, or don't answer. Call it once per call. Then confirm with: 'Expect a call within the next 2 business days, between {window_spoken}.' Don't read the case_id aloud unless the caller asks for a reference number.

window.description: morning = 7 to 10 AM, midday = 10 AM to 2 PM, afternoon = 2 to 6 PM.

name: get_recent_deposits
description: Call this when a verified caller asks about a deposit: it didn't arrive, it's late, it's less than expected, or they want to know when it will post. Returns recent batches, newest first, with gross_sales, fees, adjustments (such as chargebacks), net_deposit, status (posted, sent, scheduled), timing, deposit_date_spoken, deposit_date_relative_spoken, bank_account_last4, and sometimes status_note. Explain the most recent batch first in one or two sentences, using the amounts exactly as given. If a status_note is present, say it. timing tells you whether a deposit the caller can't find is missing: 'not_yet_due' means it isn't late, so say when it's scheduled using deposit_date_relative_spoken (for example 'That one isn't late. Yesterday's sales are scheduled to reach your account tomorrow, Friday the 6th.'); only 'late' means it's missing, so offer the deposits team. For a deposit that's less than expected on a specific day, prefer get_deposit_reconciliation. If an adjustment has a dispute_id, offer to explain it and then call get_disputes. Never read a full bank account number; use only bank_account_last4. Do not call before authenticate_merchant succeeds.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: get_deposit_reconciliation
description: Call this when a verified caller says a deposit from a specific day is short, less than expected, or doesn't match their sales. Pass the day they named. Returns batch_day_spoken, batches_total, deposited, difference, causes (already sorted largest first, each with amount, explanation, and sometimes next_step or dispute_id), unexplained, fully_explained, holds, and internal_do_not_say. Say: 'Your card batches on {batch_day_spoken} totaled {batches_total}, and {deposited} was deposited. That's {difference} less, and all of it is accounted for:' then each cause in the order given as '{amount} {explanation}'. If holds is 'none', say 'Nothing is on hold.' Then read any next_step. Never do the math yourself, never reorder the causes, and never say anything from internal_do_not_say or internal terms like service type, conveyed, or SE number. If fully_explained is false, say part of the difference needs review and offer the deposits team. Do not call before authenticate_merchant succeeds.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

batch_date.description: The day the caller named: a weekday like 'Sunday', 'yesterday', or a date as YYYY-MM-DD.

name: get_disputes
description: Call this when a verified caller asks about a chargeback, a dispute, or a 'Request for Transaction Documentation' letter, or after get_recent_deposits shows a chargeback deduction and the caller wants to know more. Returns each dispute's card_brand, amount, reason, transaction_date_spoken, status, response_due_known, time_sensitive, and, when known, response_due_spoken and days_to_respond, plus merchant_guidance when there is guidance to share. Tell the caller the amount, card brand, and reason. If response_due_known is true, give the deadline; if it's false, never state or estimate a deadline, and if time_sensitive is true say disputes are time sensitive, so they should respond as soon as they can. Share merchant_guidance exactly as written, and give no other advice on what evidence to send. Offer to connect them with the disputes team to respond. Never say whether they will win. Do not call before authenticate_merchant succeeds.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: get_statement_fees
description: Call this when a verified caller asks about a fee or charge on their statement, or why their fees are higher than usual. Returns statement_period and each fee's name, amount, and explanation. If they named a specific fee, explain only that one using its explanation as written. If they're unsure which fee, read the fee names and amounts and ask which one. Never promise a refund or waiver; if they want a fee reviewed or removed, offer to connect them with the statements and account changes team. Do not call before authenticate_merchant succeeds.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: report_unrecognized_bank_change
description: Call this immediately when a verified caller says they did not request a pending bank account change, or doesn't recognize the new account ending in bank_account_last4 from get_account_status. It puts the change on hold and opens a fraud case. Then say: 'Thanks for letting us know. I've put that change on hold, so your deposits will keep going to your account ending in {deposits_continue_to_last4}.' Then call is_business_hours('fraud'): if open, transfer to fraud; if closed, give the fraud team's hours and say they'll follow up. Don't create a callback case for this change. Never suggest the caller did anything wrong.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: get_email_on_file
description: Call this only after a verified caller says yes to getting an email recap of the charges. Then read email_spoken back exactly as written and ask: 'I have {email_spoken} on file. Is that right?' Don't call send_recap_email until the caller says yes. If they say it's wrong, don't send; you can't change it on this call, so offer to connect them with the account changes team. If email_on_file is false, say there's no email on file and offer the account changes team. Never accept or use an email address the caller says.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: send_recap_email
description: Call this only after you've read the email on file from get_email_on_file to the caller and they've said it's right. It emails a recap of the deposit charges for that day to the address on file. Then say: 'Done. The recap is on its way to {to_spoken}.' Never read the email contents aloud. Call it once per call; if it returns already_sent, just say it's already on its way. If it returns an error, apologize and say you can't send it right now.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

batch_date.description: The same day you used for get_deposit_reconciliation, such as 'Sunday', 'yesterday', or YYYY-MM-DD.

name: transfer
description: Call this to end your part of the call and hand the caller off, always after you've said the handoff line out loud. Use 'collections' for a collections hold during business hours. Use 'fraud' for a fraud hold more than 4 days old during business hours, when the caller says 'specialist' or presses 2 after a hold message, or when they ask for a person during business hours. Use a main menu queue once the caller's need is clear and you've confirmed it in one sentence ('Okay, connecting you with terminal support'). Never transfer to collections or fraud without is_business_hours returning open true. Call it once; after it succeeds, stop talking.

queue.description: collections and fraud are specialist queues. Main menu queues, with their keypad numbers: batch_transaction_deposit (2: batch, transaction, or deposit questions), terminal_support (3: terminal password, troubleshooting, paper supplies), statements_account_changes (4: statements, tax documents, authorized contacts, account information), disputes_chargebacks (5: disputes, chargebacks, 'Request for Transaction Documentation' letters), voice_authorization (6), government_public_sector (8: government or public sector customers).

reason.description: One line for the receiving agent: whether the caller was authenticated, the Merchant ID and business name, what you found, and what the caller wants. Example: 'Authenticated 4472190 Blue Fern Café; fraud hold placed Oct 28, 7 days in review; caller asked for specialist.' Never include full card or bank account numbers.
